   - y will be competitive
   - I might have an advantage at w due to my high priority
   - z could be less competitive

3. My neutral risk attitude suggests I should balance my true preferences with strategic positioning.

4. Since I have high priority at w and it's my top preference, I want to maintain w as my first choice.

5. z is my second preference and I have decent priority (2), so it makes sense to rank it second.

6. I'll place y third to potentially leverage its popularity but not overcommit.

7. x remains my least preferred, so it stays last.

This strategy maximizes my chances of getting a preferred school while being true to my original preferences.
